brief.topic: Is your AI feature ready to launch?
brief.audience: PMs preparing to launch AI features

coreInsight: An AI feature is ready to launch only when its eval passes a bar set in advance, red-team cases are handled, a fallback works, monitoring is live and rollback is tested; any “no” shrinks the launch.

hooks.text: Can you turn it off in 5 minutes?
hooks.notes: A concrete test most teams can’t answer yes to; opens the full launch gate.

hooks.text: Five yeses before an AI feature ships.
“The demo works” is not a launch criterion.
hooks.notes: Good tension but close to earlier demo-vs-eval reels.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): a specific, uncomfortable question that leads straight into the five-part launch gate.

scenes.purpose: The questions and the decision rule.
scenes.onScreen: THE LAUNCH GATE / Ship only if all five are yes. / Eval set passes a bar set before testing · Red-team prompts tried, worst ones fixed · Fallback works when the model fails or times out · Dashboards and alerts live on day one · Kill switch tested, with a named owner / One “no” means a smaller rollout, not a full launch.

caption.opening: If you can’t turn your AI feature off in five minutes, it isn’t ready to launch.
body:
The launch gate: ship only if all five are yes.
→ Eval set passes a bar you set before testing
→ Red-team prompts tried, worst ones fixed
→ Fallback works when the model fails or times out
→ Dashboards and alerts live on day one
→ Kill switch tested, with a named owner
One “no” doesn’t cancel the launch. It shrinks it: staff only, an opt-in beta, or blocked until the kill switch exists.

claims.text: AI features should pass an eval bar, red-team testing, a working fallback, live monitoring and a tested rollback before full launch; gaps call for a limited rollout.
